evidence_grade_note: Every row is a verbatim source line at a frozen commit, located by regex and re-derivable with `gap_refs.py verify`. This is a code-read of the cited line, not a claim about numerical accuracy of the upstream code.

gpusph.why: only surveyed code that combines MPI domain decomposition with a volume-based semi-analytical (SA) boundary model and an SPS/k-epsilon turbulence closure -- one source per open gap.

jax-sph.why: density-diffusion (delta-SPH) and Riemann-solver formulations plus a ghost-wall boundary condition, all in <=700 lines of readable Python and shipped with a validation harness + reference data.

salva.why: the only surveyed DFSPH *and* IISPH projection pair with explicit divergence/density-error stopping criteria -- the acceptance variable of GAP-SPH-ISPH-PROJECTION.

claims.statement: MPI world size/rank are taken at start-up and every device is mapped to a global (rank, dev) pair, so a domain can span nodes.
claims.port_recipe: TensorSPH would need the same global-device indexing before any halo exchange can be addressed.

claims.quote: void NetworkManager::sendBuffer(unsigned char src_globalDevIdx, unsigned char dst_globalDevIdx, unsigned int count, void *src_data)
claims.statement: Halo exchange is an explicit point-to-point byte-buffer send (count, void* src_data), not a collective.
claims.port_recipe: Halo payload for TensorSPH = particle SoA slice; message = raw bytes, so the same routine serves float32 and float64.

claims.quote: int mpi_err = MPI_Recv(dst_data, count, MPI_BYTE, GlobalData::RANK(src_globalDevIdx), tag, MPI_COMM_WORLD, &status);
claims.statement: The matching receive lands the halo directly into the destination device buffer (zero extra copy inside the manager).
claims.port_recipe: Mirror the send/recv pair over a dict of (src,dst) -> buffer handles.

claims.statement: All inter-rank traffic is funnelled through one object that owns the tag space and the device-pair routing.
claims.port_recipe: Single choke point is what makes the 1-rank/2-rank equivalence test inspectable; keep TensorSPH's exchange in one module too.

claims.quote: //! Auxiliary structures and functions for SA_BOUNDARY boundary conditions kernels
claims.statement: Boundary treatment is isolated in its own kernel translation unit specialised to SA_BOUNDARY (semi-analytical walls), i.e. one selectable boundary model, not a hard-wired plane reflection.
claims.port_recipe: TensorSPH can add a volume-weighted boundary module behind the same interface its Adami extrapolation uses today.

claims.quote: /// Specific variables used in neibsInCell with SA boundary
claims.statement: Boundary particles are counted in the neighbour list with a dedicated per-particle fluid+boundary counter, which is what volume-weighted boundary forces need.
claims.port_recipe: Requires the neighbour structure to distinguish fluid vs boundary neighbours; TensorSPH's neighbours3 currently does not.

claims.statement: The SA boundary path optionally carries k-epsilon turbulence state alongside the wall data.
claims.port_recipe: Boundary data and turbulence state must be co-located for wall functions; a separate array per rank would break locality.

claims.statement: Alternative reference: ghost-wall boundary conditions implemented as a velocity/pressure mirror rather than as boundary particles.
claims.port_recipe: Cheapest boundary upgrade for TensorSPH (no new particle class); Akinci is only needed when wall shear accuracy dominates.

claims.statement: DFSPH exposes min/max pressure-iteration bounds as public solver state (defaults 1/50), i.e. the projection is an iterative fixed-point with explicit termination.
claims.port_recipe: TensorSPH's acceptance wants density fluctuation <=1e-3; the number of iterations that buys it must be a reported quantity, not a constant.

claims.statement: DFSPH stops on a *divergence* error threshold (default 0.1) -- a different stopping variable from WCSPH's acoustic density error.
claims.port_recipe: The GAP acceptance should report residual divergence, not only rho/rho0.

claims.statement: The sibling IISPH solver instead stops on average density error (default 0.05), giving the two standard incompressibility criteria side by side.
claims.port_recipe: Pick one criterion per benchmark; mixing them hides the accuracy gain.

claims.statement: IISPH is re-exported from the same pressure-solver module that exports DFSPHSolver, so switching projection is a type change.
claims.port_recipe: Mirror as a strategy object in TensorSPH rather than a branch in the time-integration loop.

claims.statement: Sub-particle-scale stresses are carried as an explicit tau array, filled only when the SPS_STORE_TAU flag is set.
claims.port_recipe: SPS-LES in TensorSPH needs one extra per-particle tensor field, allocated on demand to keep the WCSPH path unchanged.

claims.statement: The turbulence closure is a compile-time template parameter resolved per viscosity spec, i.e. the model is a policy of the force kernel.
claims.port_recipe: Same policy pattern keeps TensorSPH's kernel-type dispatch (a hot path) branch-free.

claims.quote: rho * ops.segment_sum(temp, i_s, N) + c_ref * delta * support * diff_term
claims.statement: delta-SPH density evolution: the continuity sum gets an additive c_ref*delta*support*diff_term -- a diffusion term that suppresses the acoustic floor without any projection step.
claims.port_recipe: Cheapest partial answer to the WCSPH noise documented in verification_startup_quiescence.md: ~2 lines in the density update, with delta as a tunable (default 0.1 in jax-sph defaults.py).

claims.statement: Riemann-solver formulation (Zhang 2017 eq. 7): an interface star velocity built from the pressure jump, i.e. dissipative upwinding inside the density evolution instead of an added diffusion term.
claims.port_recipe: Two mutually exclusive accuracy levers; TensorSPH should benchmark delta-SPH first (no EOS change) and Riemann second.

claims.statement: Each validation case is a function comparing a run against a closed-form/reference series (here Taylor-Green at two resolutions), i.e. the repository ships its own reference-value harness.
claims.port_recipe: Directly reusable pattern for the benchmark judge that TensorSPH benchmarks still lack.

claims.statement: Kernel family is a class with analytic w and grad_w per dimensionality, so a new kernel is a class, not an if-branch.
claims.port_recipe: TensorSPH kernel3.py already has the same shape -- confirms the design, no action.

claims.statement: Boundary kernels are renormalised by their Shepard divisor with a 0.1*gamma floor guard -- the numerical core of a volume-weighted boundary, where the wall must not divide by a near-empty neighbourhood.
claims.port_recipe: Any volume boundary in TensorSPH needs this guard, otherwise the first wall layer spikes on re-entry.

claims.statement: The divergence-free projection exits only when the mean residual divergence is under threshold *and* the minimum iteration count is met -- the concrete form of the criterion GAP-SPH-ISPH-PROJECTION must report.
claims.port_recipe: TensorSPH's acceptance test can reuse this exit criterion and log (avg_err, iterations) per step.

gaps_not_covered.GAP-SPH-MULTIPHASE-SHARP: none of the three wave-3 repositories implements a sharpening multiphase scheme; the wave-2 DualSPHysics and SPlisHSPlasH deep dives are the relevant references, so no new code evidence is claimed here.
